evidence: STATIC DESIGN (no defect found): Reward is shaped, not binary. task/tests/scoring.toml: gates render=0.0, constraints=0.0 (zero mass), weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2, floors functional=0.05; identical to the frozen template scoring.toml and score.py (diff clean). score.py computes weighted = sum(w*score)/sum(w) and only zeroes on gate failure or functional<=0.05. Functional (scored/functional/judge.toml, aggregation weighted_mean) has 44 independent binary criteria, total weight 59.5, max single share 2.5/59.5=4.2% (hro_stale_refused, hro_live_board, hro_candidate_private), min 0.5/59.5=0.84%. Polish has 5 binary criteria (weights 3,3,2,1.5,2.5 of 12; weighted_mean). Visual has 5 likert criteria points=5 with anchors at every level (weight 1.2 each), giving 5 gradations each. Anti-collapse wording: functional prompt.md line 13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own'; line 23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'; polish prompt line 12 and visual prompt line 32 likewise say judge each criterion independently. The only all-or-nothing preconditions are the two gates (minimal sign-in render; job+candidate created and read back from an independent Observer context) and the functional/polish in-suite repeat of that same minimal backend check, which a dead/static app should fail and which a partial real app passes. Hand-computed spread for plausible partial apps (illustrative arithmetic only, not measured): (a) board-only app with rules but no conversations/candidate portal loses ~20.5/59.5 functional (T/U/K rows incl. candidate_no_staff/candidate_private which zero without the candidate's own data) -> F~0.66; polish ~0.25 if live board works; visual e.g. 0.6 -> reward ~0.56. (b) CRUD board with no server-side refusals (skips, places, roles, stale, all-or-none) loses most M/L/R/B refusal rows -> F roughly 0.3-0.45, reward ~0.3-0.45. (c) Polling-without-push app loses live_board/msg_exchange/unread/scrolled_up/seen (9.5/59.5=16% functional) and polish live_board+live_thread (6/12) -> visibly lower but nonzero. (d) Minimal job+candidate app passing only job_open/add_candidate/email_rules/move_one_stage (3.5/59.5=0.059 > 0.05 floor) earns ~0.035+visual/polish share -> near floor. These show the rubric is structurally capable of a graded spread with no single criterion dominating. MISSING MEASUREMENT (why not Pass): Row 40 asks whether the rubric PRODUCES a spread across partial-quality apps. raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only runtime evidence is a scripted golden Playwright/API driver (workspace.cjs, 25 groups), which is not a configured judge run and contains no mutated weak apps. REVIEW_POLICY.md requires hash-bound reward-discrimination records before clearance; the skill forbids upgrading an unmeasured claim to Pass. Residual risks that only a run can settle: (1) workload: functional is a single batched judge with timeout 9000 and a very long ordered protocol (Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D); if budget is exhausted, every later protocol's rows become 'NOT EXERCISED' binary 0 for strong and weak apps alike, compressing the spread toward the early-protocol rows; (2) the in-suite global gate (functional prompt line 11-13; polish line 9-12; visual line 29-32) zeroes a whole suite on one observed failure, so a flaky independent-context step can collapse a suite for an otherwise working app; (3) judge-level collapse of many binary rows on a weaker judge model is unmeasured.
counterexample: Plausible broken app that could pass: none found that the static rubric would score at the top — dead/static/seed-copy apps fail the constraints gate (independent Observer readback of a newly created job+candidate). Conforming alternative that could be graded all-or-nothing: a fully conforming but slow-to-drive app whose functional judge exhausts the 9000 s budget around protocol B would score 0 on all later T/U/K/R/V/A/D rows exactly like a broken app, flattening discrimination; unmeasured, so recorded as risk not as Fail.
suggested_fix: Obtain hash-bound reward-discrimination evidence: run the full configured verifier on the golden plus at least 2-3 mutated partial apps (e.g. no live push; no server-side stage/places/role refusals; no conversations) and record per-dimension and final rewards showing an ordered spread; also record full functional judge duration against the 9000 s budget.
